newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania plans to raise 500 mln DM in bonds - agency.
newsitem.headline: Romania plans to raise 500 mln DM in bonds - agency.

text.p: Romania's Finance Ministry plans to launch a bond issue of around 500 million DM, its first international raising, in about two months, independent news agency Mediafax quoted a ministry official as saying.
Junior finance minister Ionut Costea said his ministry had invited major investment banks, including CS First Boston .ROSI, Merrill Lynch, JP Morgan and Deutsche Bank, to offer advice on the issue.

Costea was speaking in Washington, where he accompanied the Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara, and they were due in Bucharest later on Thursday. Ministry officials were not immediately available to comment.
Mediafax said the banks were expected to reply to the finance ministry's request on Thursday.

After an absence of more than a decade, Romania re-entered international capital markets in 1995 with syndicated loans for the National Bank (central bank), which also launched the first Samurai and Eurobond issues last year.

Romania won its first credit ratings from major agencies in March 1996. Japan Credit Rating agency awarded it a BB-plus, as opposed to the BB-minus ratings of Standard and Poor's and IBCA and BA-three from Moody's Investors Service.
The new centrist coalition government, which ousted ex-communists in last November's elections, has embarked on a shock therapy programme to try to win international financial support.

The International Monetary Fund is expected to approve a $400 million, one-year stand-by loan to back up Romania's reforms in mid-April. The World Bank is slated to lend another $600 million for worker retraining and support for farmers.

Earlier this year central bank governor Mugur Isarescu said his bank plans to raise up to $1.6 billion in 1997 and to seek better terms for its international borrowing. The BNR borrowed around $1.4 billion from world markets last year when it serviced debt payments of around $1.2 billion.
This week parliament's lower house approved a ceiling of $3.2 billion for international lonas raised by the central bank and finance ministry this year.
Two large Romanian companies have launched international corporate bonds this year, while several other firms and municipalities announced plans to raise funds from the international capital markets.
Latest data put Romania's total foreign exchange reserves, including some 88 tonnes of gold, at $2.77 billion in January.
Romania's medium- and long-term external debt was $6.9 billion last year. External debt servicing is estimated at some $1.5 billion in 1997.
